paper_title: Fused Audio Instance and Representation for Respiratory Disease Detection
our_auroc_result: Clean fold-local multimodal AUROC 0.8489 +/- 0.0195; fixed top-800 sensitivity AUROC 0.8641 +/- 0.0195.
professor_facing_interpretation: Under the fixed-feature setting our AUROC was numerically almost identical to FAIR. The cleaner fold-local estimate remained within 1.69 percentage points.
essential_caveat: The fixed-feature result is a sensitivity analysis because feature ranking was not repeated inside every fold. Cohort snapshot, representations, and testing design differ.

paper_title: Multi-Modal Point-of-Care Diagnostics for COVID-19 Based on Acoustics and Symptoms
venue: IEEE Journal of Translational Engineering in Health and Medicine
our_auroc_result: Clean fold-local multimodal AUROC 0.8489; fixed top-800 sensitivity AUROC 0.8641; primary equal-weight participant-split AUROC 0.8949; exploratory stack AUROC 0.8971.
auroc_gap_percentage_points: Against three-audio 0.880: clean -3.11 points; fixed sensitivity -1.59 points; primary split +1.49 points.
professor_facing_interpretation: Our conventional multimodal audio result was reasonably close to their audio-only fusion. The primary internal result was numerically higher, but it came from a different evaluation design.
essential_caveat: Their 0.963 includes symptoms and must never be compared with our audio-only fusion. Neither source-split result is protocol-matched to their result.

paper_title: COVID-19 Detection From Respiratory Sounds With Hierarchical Spectrogram Transformers
venue: IEEE Journal of Biomedical and Health Informatics
our_auroc_result: Clean Coswara multimodal AUROC 0.8489; fixed-feature sensitivity AUROC 0.8641; primary Coswara equal-weight multimodal AUROC 0.8949; exploratory stack AUROC 0.8971.
auroc_gap_percentage_points: Nominal gaps: clean -5.11 points; fixed sensitivity -3.59 points; primary split -0.51 points.
professor_facing_interpretation: Our primary internal AUROC was numerically close to HST, while the cleaner repeated-CV estimates were lower. A completed HST reproduction would be required for an architecture-matched comparison.
essential_caveat: HST used an internal COUGHVID cough task. Our values use Coswara multimodal audio. The nominal gaps are not apples-to-apples performance differences.

paper_title: Robust COVID-19 Detection From Cough Sounds Using Deep Neural Decision Tree and Forest: A Comprehensive Cross-Datasets Evaluation
paper_auroc_result: Coswara internal cough AUC 0.920; COUGHVID internal AUC 0.930; Coswara-to-COUGHVID transfer AUC 0.530.
our_auroc_result: Matched Coswara cough source AUROC 0.8494 to 0.8679; frozen COUGHVID external AUROC 0.5226 to 0.5428 across four model families.
auroc_gap_percentage_points: Internal Coswara gap: -7.06 to -5.21 points; external transfer gap: -0.74 to +1.28 points.
professor_facing_interpretation: Their model was clearly stronger internally, but their 0.530 transfer AUROC falls inside our 0.5226 to 0.5428 external range. Independent pipelines therefore showed essentially the same cross-dataset discrimination failure.
essential_caveat: Their selected cohorts, label definitions, participant grouping, and target composition differ from ours. Similar external AUROC does not establish statistical equivalence.

paper_title: Sounds of COVID-19: Exploring Realistic Performance of Audio-Based Digital Testing
paper_auroc_result: Controlled multimodal AUC-ROC 0.710 with 95% CI 0.650 to 0.770; biased settings reached 0.900 with 95% CI 0.850 to 0.950.
our_auroc_result: Conventional multimodal AUROC 0.8489 clean and 0.8641 fixed-feature sensitivity; primary internal AUROC 0.8949; temporal multi-seed AUROC 0.6908 +/- 0.0066.
auroc_gap_percentage_points: Temporal versus controlled: -1.92 points; primary internal versus biased: -0.51 points.
professor_facing_interpretation: Our favorable internal and strict temporal scores reproduce the broad pattern that AUROC depends strongly on cohort construction and validation design.
essential_caveat: Different datasets and controls prevent direct model ranking. Their intervals are 95% confidence intervals, while our +/- values are fold or seed standard deviations.

paper_title: Audio-Based AI Classifiers Show No Evidence of Improved COVID-19 Screening Over Simple Symptoms Checkers
paper_auroc_result: Unadjusted ROC-AUC 0.846 with 95% CI 0.838 to 0.854; matched ROC-AUC 0.619 with 95% CI 0.594 to 0.644.
our_auroc_result: Clean conventional AUROC 0.8489; fixed-feature sensitivity AUROC 0.8641; temporal multi-seed AUROC 0.6908; frozen external AUROC 0.5226 to 0.5428.
auroc_gap_percentage_points: Against unadjusted 0.846: clean +0.29 points; fixed sensitivity +1.81 points. Other gaps are not direct comparisons.
professor_facing_interpretation: Our conventional internal AUROC is in the same numerical range as their unadjusted result. Both studies show that stronger controls produce substantially less favorable estimates.
essential_caveat: Their large PCR-referenced UK cohort and matched analysis are methodologically stronger. Our temporal and external rows are not equivalent to their confounder-matched endpoint.

paper_title: A Comprehensive Drift-Adaptive Framework for Sustaining Model Performance in COVID-19 Detection From Dynamic Cough Audio Data: Model Development and Validation
paper_auroc_result: Coswara AUC-ROC decreased from 0.668 to 0.597; COVID-19 Sounds decreased from 0.691 to 0.607 under postdevelopment evaluation.
our_auroc_result: Primary internal AUROC 0.8949; temporal multi-seed AUROC 0.6908 +/- 0.0066; early-versus-late top-800 feature Jaccard overlap 0.074.
auroc_gap_percentage_points: No fair head-to-head AUROC gap; both studies show temporal degradation.
professor_facing_interpretation: Their results establish degradation in chronological postdevelopment data. Our work adds a higher-capacity internal model, repeated-seed temporal evaluation, very low temporal feature overlap, and independent external transfer.
essential_caveat: Their work implements drift detection and adaptation. Our analysis is retrospective, and the internal and temporal rows do not form a pure one-model one-cohort paired comparison.
